The data looks like the Sachs et al. flow-cytometry set. In the data, pmek and pjnk are only weakly correlated (r ≈ 0.22). pjnk is much more strongly tied to PKC (r ≈ 0.81) and P38 (r ≈ 0.80). In the known signalling network, PKC drives both pmek and pjnk, so their weak correlation comes from that shared upstream cause and not from a direct link. I did not test this with a causal-discovery method. The answer rests on the correlations and on that known network.

ANSWER: C
